_comment: QI Task Health Manifest — the outcome-based counterpart to scheduled_tasks_window_policy.json. That file decides how a task runs; THIS file decides how we know it actually worked. Created 2026-08-27 by the scheduled-task health audit, which found 7 tasks silently dead (TubeScout for 66 days) while Task Scheduler reported success for every one of them. Evaluated by C:\QIH\tools\qi_task_health.py, hosted in the always-on QI_TaskHealth service.
_why_not_lasttaskresult: 24 of 37 QI tasks are wrapped in `conhost.exe --headless`, which returns exit code 0 even when the wrapped binary does not exist. LastTaskResult is meaningless for those.
_why_not_mtime: A wrapper log's mtime proves only that SOMETHING appended. Task actions redirect with '>> log 2>&1', so the shell's own failure messages land in the log meant to prove success. During the 18-day OC outage Yubin's wrapper log grew EVERY DAY with 'No such file or directory' while the job was completely dead. Prefer db > marker > git > file, in that order.

_check_types.sqlite: query must return a single timestamp; freshest wins. Strongest check — a real data row.
_check_types.marker: a success string must appear in a log file whose name may contain {date:FMT}. Proves the job reached its own finish line.
_check_types.git: most recent commit timestamp in a repo.
_check_types.file: artifact mtime. Weakest — use only where nothing better exists.

_severity: high = tell me the day it breaks. medium = tell me, no rush. low = report only.

QI_TubeScout_AM.note: THE case study. Dead 2026-06-22 -> 2026-08-27 (66 days) on an expired Google OAuth refresh token, while logging 'cycle done' twice daily and feeding Kaze a corpus with zero new input. Nothing was watching it. Root cause: the Cloud OAuth consent screen is in Testing status, so refresh tokens hard-expire after 7 days.

QI_TubeScout_PM.note: Same artifact as the AM run — either firing keeps it fresh.

OC-Kaze-Digest-6AM.note: Generalised from check_digest_freshness() in oc-keepalive-daemon.py — the reference implementation this whole manifest is modelled on.

OC-Yubin-Daily-8AM.note: Written on EVERY run including zero-email days, so absence is unambiguous. Was frozen at 2026-08-09 07:00:33 for 18 days while its wrapper log kept growing with failures — the exact case that disproves mtime-of-log checking.

OC-Asa-Briefing-7AM.note: Uses Asa's own dated log, not the append-only wrapper asa-task.log. The wrapper log captured 18 days of 'No such file or directory' and kept looking fresh the entire time — it is exactly the signal that must not be trusted.

OC-Kakei-Weekly-Sunday-7PM.note: Weekly (Sun 19:00), so glob-newest rather than today's date. Until 2026-08-27 this printed its success line WITHOUT checking curl's response — 11 of 11 runs had actually failed on a JSONDecodeError. The marker is only trustworthy because that check now exists.

OC-Sentry-Drift-Sunday-8PM.note: Weekly. Had NEVER produced a report since creation — it read a reports dir that never existed and exited 0 on a 'skipping (no error)' guard. Fixed 2026-08-27 via inspector_export_snapshot.py; first successful drift report in its life ran that day.

QI_NightlyGitSync.note: ABORTed on C:\APPS\PersonalSong every night from 2026-07-02 on a staged plex_token. It logged the ABORT correctly every single time — nobody read it. Alerting is the missing half, not logging.

MaiaNightlySync.note: Checks a real commit, not the log, because this task used to write 'Nothing staged - skipping commit' and exit 0 while 86 files went unbacked for ~2 months.

QI_EffortLedger_Daily.note: Gold standard artifact: a hash-chained, tamper-evident row. Every unattended job should aim for something this unambiguous.

QI_BrainBackfill.note: Every 30 min; 2h window tolerates a couple of misses.

QI_McpConnectorGuard.note: Every 5 min; already self-warns past 15 min via --status.

QI_ClaudeUpdate_6AM.note: Silent-by-design on days with no pending update, but it POSITIVELY DECLARES that by writing result:'noop' to this ledger every morning. That is the pattern every quiet job should copy — it is why 'nothing happened' is still provably healthy here.

QI_UsageSnapshot.note: pythonw, so its LastTaskResult IS trustworthy — included anyway because outcome beats exit code.

QI_TaskHealth.note: The monitor watching itself. It rewrites this file every pass (every 30 min), so a stale one means the monitor stopped. Without this entry a dead monitor would look exactly like a healthy estate - silence reading as success, which is the failure mode this whole manifest exists to eliminate.

TubeScout_SubsRefresh.query: SELECT value FROM state WHERE key='last_subs_refresh'
TubeScout_SubsRefresh.note: NOT a scheduled task - a drift watch. TubeScout's sweep moved to an API key on 2026-08-27 (API keys never expire; the OAuth token died after 7 days and cost 66 days of silence). The only step still needing OAuth is pull_subscriptions(), which runs manually. If this goes stale, newly subscribed channels are being silently ignored. Fix: cd /d C:\APPS\TUBESCOUT && python -m shared.sweep --pull-subs
